subtopics.title: Plot the tangent graph
subtopics.exposition: The dashed vertical lines drawn at the values of θ where tan θ is not defined are called the asymptotes. For any value of θ, tan θ = sin θ / cos θ. For values of θ for which sin θ = 0, tan θ = 0 as well. If cos θ = 0, the value of tan θ is undefined, because we cannot divide by 0. The table of values for tan θ gives 0 at 0°, 0.58 at 30°, 1 at 45°, 1.73 at 60°, undefined at 90°, -1.73 at 120°, -1 at 135°, -0.58 at 150° and 0 at 180°. To plot y = tan θ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, use a calculator to complete a table of values of tan θ. After completing the table, plot the points and join them with a smooth curve. On the graph of y = tan θ for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, mark the asymptotes as the lines θ = 90° and θ = 270°, where tan θ is undefined. The values of tan θ in the table are rounded to 2 decimal places. Choose an appropriate scale and plot θ on the x-axis and tan θ on the y-axis.

subtopics.title: Sketch a tan θ + q
subtopics.exposition: The effect of q is called a vertical shift: the whole tangent graph shifts up or down by q units. For q > 0, the graph is shifted vertically upwards by q units. For q < 0, the graph is shifted vertically downwards by q units. The value of a affects the steepness of each of the branches of the graph. The greater the value of a, the quicker the branches of the graph approach the asymptotes. For y = 2 tan θ + 1, the table gives y = 1 at 0°, 2.15 at 30°, 4.46 at 60°, no value at 90°, -2.46 at 120°, -0.15 at 150° and 1 at 180°. To investigate the effects of a and q, plot several tangent graphs on the same set of axes for 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, varying q (with a = 1) in one set and a in another, and compare the results. To sketch y = a tan θ + q, first examine the standard form of the equation to see the values of a and q. Seeing a > 1 tells you the branches of the curve will be steeper. Seeing q > 0 tells you the graph is shifted vertically upwards by q units (1 unit for y = 2 tan θ + 1). Substitute values of θ from 0° to 360° into the equation to complete a table of y-values. Plot the points of the table and join them with a smooth curve to sketch y = 2 tan θ + 1.

subtopics.title: Tangent graph characteristics
subtopics.exposition: A period of 180° means that one tangent cycle is completed in 180°. The y-intercept of f(θ) = a tan θ + q is the value of f(θ) at θ = 0°. tan θ is undefined at θ = 90° and θ = 270°. The domain of the tangent graph is {θ : 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, θ ≠ 90°; 270°}. The range of the tangent graph is {f(θ) : f(θ) ∈ ℝ}. The period of y = a tan θ + q is 180°. The graph has asymptotes at θ = 90° and θ = 270°. For y = tan θ, the x-intercepts are (0°, 0), (180°, 0) and (360°, 0). For y = tan θ, the y-intercept is (0°, 0). For y = 2 tan θ + 1 the domain is {θ : 0° ≤ θ ≤ 360°, θ ≠ 90°; 270°}. For y = 2 tan θ + 1 the range is {f(θ) : f(θ) ∈ ℝ}.

subtopics.title: Find a and q from graph
subtopics.exposition: The y-intercept of y = a tan θ + q is the point (0°, q), so the y-value of that point is q. To find the y-intercept of f(θ) = a tan θ + q, put θ = 0°: a tan 0° + q = a(0) + q = q.
